name: Vercel Sandbox
oneLiner: Firecracker microVMs inside Vercel, billed on active CPU and provisioned memory.
whatItIs: Vercel Sandbox runs untrusted or agent-generated code in Firecracker microVMs, managed through a CLI, JavaScript SDK or Python SDK.
It is part of the Vercel platform rather than a separate product: usage sits on the Vercel plan, and the Hobby plan is restricted to non-commercial use.
whoFor: Teams already on Vercel who want agent code execution with many regions and familiar account controls.
isolation: Firecracker microVM with a dedicated kernel. Root access, Docker and FUSE are documented; systemd and nested virtualisation are not.
sizes: 1 or even numbers of vCPUs from 2 to 32 depending on plan, 2 GB of memory per vCPU, and 64 GB of ephemeral NVMe. Hobby caps at 4 vCPU / 8 GB, Pro at 8 / 16, Enterprise at 32 / 64. Nineteen regions; no GPU published.

billing.model: Metered usage against the Vercel plan, with a monthly credit on Pro.
billing.meter: Active CPU at $0.128 per CPU-hour, excluding time waiting on I/O; provisioned memory at $0.0212 per GB-hour with a one-minute minimum; creations, data transfer, snapshots and drives separately.
billing.stopped: No CPU or memory charge, but snapshots and drives keep billing. Persistent sandboxes create a billable snapshot when they stop.
billing.planFee: Vercel Pro is $20 a month and includes $20 of usage credit, which expires monthly.
billing.minimum: Memory bills in one-minute increments. Hobby has included quotas and pauses creation when they are exhausted.

A.headline: $18.40 before credit
A.shape: 2 vCPU / 4 GB, 10% average CPU, deleted after each task
notes: An otherwise unused $20 Pro credit covers this, but the $20 platform fee remains.
Opt out of persistence, or deleting a sandbox leaves billable snapshots.

B.headline: $161.18 before credit, and not a continuous session
B.shape: 4 vCPU / 8 GB, 10% average CPU, 730 running-equivalent hours
notes: A single session cannot exceed 24 hours on Pro, so 730 hours needs restarts and snapshots.
50 GiB is not a configurable disk: the standard filesystem is 64 GB, and drives are billed on used data.
B.flag: The always-on workload breaks the 24-hour per-session limit, so this is a running-equivalent estimate rather than a feasible single sandbox.

C.headline: $9.94 before credit
C.shape: 2 vCPU / 4 GB, 10% average CPU, 90 running hours, stopped otherwise
notes: A 20 GB drive holding 20 GB of data for the month adds about $1.00 plus reads and writes.
Retaining the filesystem as snapshots adds storage; 30 stops can create 30 snapshots.

usability.dashboard: The Vercel dashboard can stop or delete a sandbox and shows a lifecycle activity log.
usability.withoutCode: No documented no-code path; the workflows are CLI and SDK.
usability.signup: A Vercel account. Card requirement depends on the plan and trial path; Hobby is non-commercial only.
usability.docs: Vercel's docs cover sandbox concepts, SDK, pricing and limits. Support follows the Vercel plan.
tripsUp: The default timeout is 5 minutes, and the maximum session is 45 minutes on Hobby, 24 hours on Pro.
Persistent sandboxes bill snapshot storage automatically.
Active CPU excludes I/O wait, so the meter is not wall-clock time.
Hobby pauses sandbox creation when quotas run out.

caveats.detail: Persistent sandboxes save their filesystem when stopped, and each automatic snapshot consumes snapshot storage billed separately from compute.

caveats.issue: The session limit is not a lifetime limit
caveats.detail: The maximum duration applies to a single session: 45 minutes on Hobby, 24 hours on Pro and Enterprise. Persistent sandboxes can be resumed into a new session.
The Hobby plan restricts users to non-commercial, personal use only.
One page says creation pauses until 30 days after first use; another says until the next billing cycle.

caveats.issue: Fork is not a live memory copy
caveats.detail: Fork uses the current saved snapshot or falls back to a fresh create from the image; manual snapshotting stops the source.

strengths: Firecracker isolation with root and Docker inside.
Credential brokering keeps secrets out of the guest.
Drives are billed on used data, not provisioned size.
Snapshots expire after 30 days by default and can be kept indefinitely.
